title: The Way You Fold a Towel
core_idea: Whatever one believes about an afterlife, the people we have lost often continue in the habits, phrases and kindnesses they passed on to us.
text: Maybe you fold towels the way your grandmother did. Maybe you hum a song your father always hummed, or say a phrase that was once only his. Small things like these can catch us off guard. Suddenly, someone who is gone feels very close. People hold many different beliefs about what happens after we die. Some trust in a life beyond this one. Some are simply not sure. But almost everyone can recognise this: the people we love leave traces in us. A way of laughing. A habit of kindness. A recipe made by heart. Next time you notice one, you might pause for a moment. In that small gesture, something of them lives on.
description: A quiet reflection on the small habits and kindnesses that carry our loved ones with us.
